title: RankSafe Prefix Cache for DINO-WM CEM Planning
title_zh: 用于 DINO-WM CEM 规划的 RankSafe 前缀缓存
hook: C$^3$ache and X-Cache use residual similarity or action-aware fingerprints as evidence that reused computation is safe, but neither makes CEM candidate ordering the target of that decision. RankSafe reframes shared-prefix caching as a planner-selection problem and reuses only an exact action-independent prefix whose downstream candidate costs are invariant by construction.
abstract_draft: Counterfactual action-sequence evaluation is the main cost in DINO-WM's CEM planner: many candidates share the same observation and history computation, yet the planner repeatedly recomputes it before applying different action-conditioned suffixes. Recent reuse methods such as C³ache (arxiv:2606.08962v1) and X-Cache (arxiv:2604.20289v2) use residual similarity or action-aware fingerprints, but they do not make preservation of CEM candidate ordering the validity target. RankSafe-EPC instruments the forward graph, identifies an exact prefix whose outputs are independent of the candidate action, computes that prefix once, and reuses it while retaining every action-conditioned suffix and a mismatch fallback. The load-bearing prediction is that a correct action-dependency mask will preserve candidate costs, CEM first-action choices, and closed-loop Wall success while reducing native end-to-end planner latency; a randomized mask should instead induce rank inversions and lower action agreement. The expected outcome is a bounded planner-level cache with an explicit invariance contract, not a claim that approximate cache similarity is safe in general. Failure to reduce native latency or failure of the randomized-mask control to affect downstream decisions would falsify the proposed mechanism.

motivation.problem_framing:
DINO-WM's test-time CEM planner evaluates multiple counterfactual action sequences from one observed history. The visual/history prefix before the action-conditioned dynamics suffix is shared across those candidates, but a naive implementation recomputes it for every branch. The bottleneck is therefore not merely model inference time: any reuse rule must preserve the ordering of candidate costs that determines the selected first action. A cache that saves FLOPs while silently changing that ordering can alter closed-loop behavior even when individual predictions look close.

C³ache and X-Cache make reuse decisions from residual similarity or action-aware fingerprints, and WorldCache uses curvature and drift to trade rollout fidelity for speed. These works establish that computation reuse is useful, but their validity signals are not an exact graph-level statement about which computation is independent of counterfactual actions. RankSafe-EPC treats the DINO-WM Wall planner as the primary instance of this gap: it isolates an action-independent prefix, leaves the suffix untouched, and tests the resulting candidate-order and first-action invariance directly.
motivation.why_now: Recent cache systems such as C³ache, X-Cache, and WorldCache make reuse practical but stop short of planner-selection invariance. The existing DINO-WM Wall checkpoint and local trajectories provide a fixed, reproducible setting in which graph instrumentation, exact-prefix reuse, native latency, and first-action agreement can be measured without retraining; 2–4 A100s are sufficient for the bounded implementation and matched evaluation. This makes the missing contract testable now, while keeping the claim explicitly provisional until native end-to-end and closed-loop evidence is obtained.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: C³ache reuses same-denoising-step residuals across smooth consecutive WAM chunks and reports task-success degradation as its main safety signal.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It did not identify an exact observation/history prefix shared by counterfactual CEM branches or test preservation of their candidate-cost ordering.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its residual-similarity construction is tied to smooth executed chunks, not an action-independence analysis of the planner's forward graph.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: X-Cache gates cross-chunk residual reuse with structure- and action-aware fingerprints while protecting persistent KV updates.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It did not certify equality of the planner-relevant prefix across a CEM candidate set or selected-action preservation under exact reuse.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Fingerprint gating supplies an approximate similarity test, whereas the missing mechanism is a graph-level action-independence contract with a planner-level consequence.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: WorldCache adapts token skipping from curvature and drift to maintain video-rollout fidelity.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It did not retain all action-conditioned suffix computation while targeting CEM candidate ranking and first-action selection.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its fidelity proxy is defined for rollout content, not for the ordering statistic that a sampling-based planner uses to select an action.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: EfficientVLA combines layer pruning, visual-token selection, and temporal action-head feature caching in CogACT.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It did not define an exact shared-prefix object or validity condition for DINO-WM's counterfactual CEM branches.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its compression changes the represented computation, so it does not isolate planner-preserving reuse by an action-dependency boundary.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: DINO-WM uses pretrained visual features and test-time action-sequence optimization for zero-shot planning.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It did not expose a reusable prefix object or a cache-validity test tied to candidate-cost and selected-action invariance.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: The original planner evaluates each counterfactual branch directly and provides no graph instrumentation for separating action-independent from action-dependent computation.

motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: A successful result would turn shared-prefix reuse into a planner-level operation with an explicit condition for preserving CEM candidate ordering and the selected first action, rather than a similarity heuristic whose downstream effect is unknown. It would also give systems such as C³ache and X-Cache a concrete diagnostic boundary for separating safe exact reuse from approximate cross-chunk reuse, while making native latency and closed-loop agreement jointly measurable.

core_claim: Caching an exactly action-independent DINO-WM prefix across CEM candidates preserves candidate-cost ordering and the selected first action, whereas corrupting its action-dependency mask causes rank inversions.

sub_claims.statement: A graph-derived binary mask can identify a DINO-WM prefix whose outputs are identical for all counterfactual CEM candidates.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the bottleneck's missing action-independence contract for shared observation/history computation.

sub_claims.statement: Reusing that exact prefix while recomputing every action-conditioned suffix preserves candidate costs, their ordering, and the CEM first-action choice.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the gap between computation reuse and the planner-selection quantity that controls downstream behavior.

sub_claims.statement: A randomized action-dependency mask produces candidate-cost rank inversions and lower first-action agreement or closed-loop success under a matched cache opportunity.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Distinguishes the causal invariance mechanism from a generic cache path or latency effect.

key_equations.description: The binary mask marks graph nodes at boundary b whose representation depends on the candidate action.
key_equations.description_zh: 二值 mask 标记边界 b 处依赖候选 action 的图节点。

key_equations.description: When the boundary is action-independent, one cached prefix representation is valid for every candidate j.
key_equations.description_zh: 当边界与 action 无关时，一个 cached prefix 表示可供全部候选 j 使用。

key_equations.description: CEM ranks candidates by their rollout cost after the shared prefix and candidate-specific suffix are evaluated.
key_equations.description_zh: CEM 根据共享 prefix 与候选专属 suffix 得到的 rollout cost 对候选排序。

key_equations.description: The mechanism check records rank disagreement and requires the selected first action to match the full recomputation.
key_equations.description_zh: 机制检查记录排序是否不一致，并要求 cached 与 full recomputation 的首 action 相同。

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: Given one DINO-WM Wall observation and a CEM candidate population, instrument the forward graph to locate the boundary before action-dependent computation and record its binary mask. Compute the observation/history prefix once and reuse it only when the mask certifies candidate independence; evaluate every action-conditioned suffix normally. Compare the cached and full candidate costs, ordering, first action, closed-loop outcome, and native end-to-end latency, with a canary mismatch fallback for the valid cache path. A matched randomized-mask control tests whether any downstream change is caused by violating the proposed invariance rather than by caching alone.

steps.title: Trace the action boundary
steps.what_changes: Instrument the DINO-WM CEM forward graph and construct `M_b`, marking which boundary outputs depend on candidate actions.
steps.why_this_step: The bottleneck is repeated shared-prefix work, and an explicit dependency mask supplies the missing exact validity condition.
steps.input: DINO-WM Wall checkpoint, observation/history input, and CEM forward graph
steps.output: Candidate-independent boundary and binary action-dependency mask `M_b`

steps.title: Cache the invariant prefix
steps.what_changes: Compute the prefix through the certified boundary once per observation/history and feed the same cached representation to all candidate-specific suffixes.
steps.why_this_step: Exact reuse removes duplicated computation without altering the action-conditioned part that determines counterfactual outcomes.
steps.output: Reusable prefix representation plus a cache-hit path

steps.title: Guard candidate evaluation
steps.what_changes: Run each action-conditioned suffix, compare a deterministic canary against the full path, and fall back on mismatch while retaining a randomized-mask negative control with fallback disabled.
steps.why_this_step: The provenance threat is that a self-contaminated gate can hide errors; an explicit canary and a matched corrupted-mask control expose that failure mode.
steps.input: Cached prefix and candidate-specific action suffixes
steps.output: Guarded cached candidate costs and negative-control costs

steps.title: Test planner invariance
steps.what_changes: Measure candidate-cost rank disagreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop success, and native end-to-end latency against matched full recomputation.
steps.why_this_step: The proposal is about preserving the planner's selection quantity, so speed without ordering and action agreement is insufficient evidence.
steps.input: Full, RankSafe, and randomized-mask candidate evaluations under identical CEM settings

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: The design chooses exact action-independence over residual similarity because the downstream object that matters is CEM's candidate ordering, not a local feature distance. It removes only the prefix provably shared by counterfactual branches and leaves the action-conditioned suffix intact, limiting the mechanism claim to a graph boundary that can be inspected. The canary fallback addresses gate provenance, while the randomized-mask arm tests whether rank changes follow the proposed dependency violation; this separates a planner-preserving cache from generic acceleration or self-contaminated reuse.

plain_motivation_en:
DINO-WM's test-time CEM planner evaluates several alternative action sequences from the same observed history. The visual and history computation before the action-dependent dynamics part is shared by these alternatives, but a straightforward implementation recomputes it for every branch. The challenge is therefore not only inference speed. Any reuse rule must keep the candidate-cost ordering unchanged, because that ordering determines the first action selected by the planner. A cache can save computation while silently changing that ordering and consequently changing closed-loop behavior, even when individual predictions appear close.

C³ache and X-Cache decide when to reuse computation using residual similarity or action-aware fingerprints, while WorldCache uses curvature and drift to trade rollout fidelity for speed. These methods show that computation reuse can be useful, but their validity signals do not state exactly which graph computation is independent of alternative actions. RankSafe-EPC addresses this gap in the DINO-WM Wall planner by isolating a prefix that is independent of the action, leaving the suffix unchanged, and directly testing whether candidate ordering and the first selected action stay the same.

Recent cache systems such as C³ache, X-Cache, and WorldCache make reuse practical but do not establish invariance of planner selection. The existing DINO-WM Wall checkpoint and local trajectories provide a fixed, reproducible setting for measuring graph instrumentation, exact-prefix reuse, native latency, and first-action agreement without retraining. A bounded implementation and matched evaluation fit within 2–4 A100s. The missing contract can therefore be tested now, while the claim remains provisional until native end-to-end and closed-loop evidence is obtained.

Earlier work stopped short for structural reasons. C³ache reuses residuals across smooth consecutive WAM chunks, rather than analyzing action independence in a planner graph. X-Cache uses approximate structure- and action-aware fingerprint gating, rather than certifying equality of a planner-relevant prefix across CEM candidates and preservation of the selected action. WorldCache targets rollout content fidelity, rather than the candidate ordering used by a sampling-based planner. EfficientVLA changes the represented computation through pruning, token selection, and feature caching, rather than isolating planner-preserving reuse at an action-dependency boundary. DINO-WM itself performs each counterfactual branch directly and does not expose a reusable prefix or a cache-validity test tied to candidate-cost and selected-action invariance.

If the gap is closed, shared-prefix reuse becomes a planner-level operation with an explicit condition for preserving CEM candidate ordering and the selected first action, instead of a similarity heuristic with an unknown downstream effect. It also gives systems such as C³ache and X-Cache a concrete boundary for distinguishing safe exact reuse from approximate cross-chunk reuse, while allowing native latency and closed-loop agreement to be measured together.
plain_motivation_zh:
DINO-WM 的 test-time CEM planner 会从同一段观测历史出发，评估多条可能的 action sequence。这些候选共享 action-conditioned dynamics 之前的 visual/history 计算，但直接实现时会为每条分支重复计算。因此，问题不只是 inference 速度：任何复用规则都必须保持候选 cost 的排序不变，因为 planner 根据这个排序决定首个 action。即使单步 prediction 看起来接近，缓存若悄悄改变了排序，closed-loop 行为也可能随之改变。

C³ache 和 X-Cache 根据 residual similarity 或 action-aware fingerprint 决定何时复用计算，WorldCache 则利用 curvature 和 drift 在 rollout fidelity 与速度之间取舍。这些工作说明复用计算是有用的，但它们的 validity signal 没有精确说明：forward graph 中哪些计算与候选 action 无关。RankSafe-EPC 在 DINO-WM Wall planner 中处理这个缺口：找出与 action 无关的 prefix，保持 suffix 不变，并直接检查 candidate ordering 和首个 selected action 是否保持不变。

近来的 cache system（如 C³ache、X-Cache 和 WorldCache）让复用更实用，但还没有建立 planner selection invariance。现有的 DINO-WM Wall checkpoint 和 local trajectories 提供了固定且可复现的环境，可以在不 retraining 的情况下测量 graph instrumentation、exact-prefix reuse、native latency 和 first-action agreement。一个受限的实现和匹配评估可以在 2–4 张 A100 上完成。因此，这个缺失的 contract 现在可以检验；不过，在取得 native end-to-end 和 closed-loop evidence 以前，结论仍是 provisional。

已有工作停在这里有结构性原因。C³ache 在平滑的连续 WAM chunk 之间复用 residual，但没有分析 planner graph 中的 action independence。X-Cache 用近似的 structure- and action-aware fingerprint gate，而没有证明 CEM 候选之间 planner-relevant prefix 相等并保持 selected action。WorldCache 针对 rollout content fidelity，而不是 sampling-based planner 用来选择 action 的候选排序。EfficientVLA 通过 pruning、token selection 和 feature caching 改变所表示的计算，并没有在 action-dependency boundary 处隔离 planner-preserving reuse。DINO-WM 本身直接计算每条 counterfactual branch，也没有提供与 candidate-cost 和 selected-action invariance 绑定的 reusable prefix 或 cache-validity test。

如果这个缺口被补上，shared-prefix reuse 就会成为一种 planner-level operation，并有明确条件来保持 CEM candidate ordering 和 selected first action，而不再只是下游影响未知的 similarity heuristic。它也会给 C³ache 和 X-Cache 这样的 system 一个具体的 diagnostic boundary，用来区分 safe exact reuse 与 approximate cross-chunk reuse，同时共同测量 native latency 和 closed-loop agreement。

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Instrument the DINO-WM CEM forward graph using the Wall checkpoint, observation/history input, and CEM graph. Build `M_b` to mark which outputs at the chosen boundary depend on candidate actions. The result is a candidate-independent boundary and a binary action-dependency mask `M_b`.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: The repeated work is the shared prefix, so an explicit dependency mask provides the exact condition for deciding whether that prefix can be reused.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: For each observation/history, compute the prefix through the certified boundary once, then send the same cached representation to every candidate-specific action-conditioned suffix. Produce a reusable prefix representation and a cache-hit path.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: Exact reuse removes duplicated computation while leaving the action-conditioned part that determines counterfactual outcomes unchanged.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Run every action-conditioned suffix. Compare a deterministic canary with the full path and fall back on a mismatch. In parallel, retain a randomized-mask negative control with fallback disabled; use the cached prefix and candidate-specific suffixes to obtain guarded cached costs and negative-control costs.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: A gate could hide an error if it is contaminated by the result it is meant to protect. The canary and the matched corrupted-mask control expose that failure mode.

plain_method_steps_en.what_to_do: Under identical CEM settings, compare full, RankSafe, and randomized-mask candidate evaluations. Measure candidate-cost rank disagreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop success, and native end-to-end latency, and report a planner-level invariance and latency verdict.
plain_method_steps_en.why_this_makes_sense: The proposal concerns the planner's selection quantity, so speed alone is not enough; ordering and action agreement must also be preserved.

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 使用 Wall checkpoint、observation/history input 和 CEM forward graph，对 DINO-WM CEM forward graph 做 instrumentation。在选定 boundary 处构造 `M_b`，标记哪些 output 依赖候选 action。结果是 candidate-independent boundary 和 binary action-dependency mask `M_b`。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 重复发生的计算是 shared prefix，因此显式 dependency mask 能提供判断这个 prefix 是否可复用的精确条件。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 对于每个 observation/history，只计算一次通过已认证 boundary 的 prefix，然后把同一个 cached representation 送入每个 candidate-specific action-conditioned suffix。得到 reusable prefix representation 和 cache-hit path。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: Exact reuse 去掉重复计算，同时保持决定 counterfactual outcome 的 action-conditioned 部分不变。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 运行每个 action-conditioned suffix。把 deterministic canary 与 full path 比较，出现 mismatch 时回退。与此同时保留一个关闭 fallback 的 randomized-mask negative control；使用 cached prefix 和 candidate-specific suffixes，得到 guarded cached costs 与 negative-control costs。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 如果 gate 被它本应保护的结果污染，它可能掩盖错误。canary 和匹配的 corrupted-mask control 可以暴露这种 failure mode。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 在相同的 CEM settings 下比较 full、RankSafe 和 randomized-mask candidate evaluations。测量 candidate-cost rank disagreement、first-action agreement、closed-loop success 以及 native end-to-end latency，并给出 planner-level invariance 和 latency verdict。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这个 proposal 关注的是 planner 的 selection quantity，因此只有速度还不够；还必须保持排序和 action agreement。

plain_method_modules_en.purpose_oneline: Identify the exact action-independent boundary and reuse the shared prefix while preserving each action-conditioned suffix.
Guard candidate evaluation and test planner invariance, downstream decisions, and native latency.

plain_method_modules_zh.purpose_oneline: 找出精确的 action-independent boundary，复用 shared prefix，同时保留每个 action-conditioned suffix。
保护 candidate evaluation，并检验 planner invariance、下游 decision 和 native latency。

falsification_prediction: The minimal experiment uses the existing DINO-WM Wall checkpoint and trajectories with identical CEM seeds, candidate population, horizon, and controller settings to compare full recomputation, RankSafe exact-prefix caching, and a negative-control cache that forcibly randomizes the action-dependency mask at the chosen boundary with fallback disabled for that control arm. The load-bearing variable is M_b, the binary action-dependency mask for the cached prefix: when M_b is correct, the cached and full runs should make the same CEM first-action choices and retain closed-loop success while native end-to-end planner latency decreases. Randomizing M_b while keeping the cache path and hit opportunity comparable should create candidate-cost rank inversions and lower first-action agreement and closed-loop success, rather than merely changing M_b itself. If exact prefix caching does not reduce native end-to-end latency, or if the randomized-mask control does not degrade downstream decisions, the planner-level invariance mechanism is falsified.
compute_budget: 2–4 A100 allocation, 12 A100-GPU-days total for graph instrumentation, CPU preparation, smoke checks, matched native latency, and closed-loop Wall evaluation; $0 API cost because the existing checkpoint and local trajectories are used; no full pretraining.
what_step_was_missed: C$^3$ache would have needed to identify and factor out the observation/history computation that is invariant across counterfactual CEM branches, then connect that exact reuse to a candidate-cost ordering and selected-action preservation test in the DINO-WM planner; its cross-chunk residual construction instead assumes smooth executed behavior and stops at task-success degradation.

compute.rationale: API line ≈ $0 vs $10000 (0%) → feasible. Overall (worse line) → feasible.

data.rationale: The existing DINO-WM Wall checkpoint and local trajectories provide the required inputs, with the public DINO-WM Wall setup as a reproducible substitute if traces must be regenerated.

theoretical.rationale: The theoretical burden is a graph-level action-independence and ordering-invariance condition that can be checked directly from the instrumented forward path without a new training theorem.

engineering.rationale: Native graph instrumentation, canary fallback, and matched end-to-end latency measurement are implementable but are the binding cost within the stated 2–4 A100 and 12 GPU-day budget.

falsification.rationale: The existing checkpoint, fixed CEM settings, randomized-mask intervention, rank and first-action metrics, and native latency path form a concrete runnable falsification test.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: C$^3$ache reuses same-denoising-step residuals across smooth consecutive WAM chunks with negligible task-success degradation, whereas RankSafe factorizes the DINO-WM CEM forward graph at an exact action-independent observation/history prefix and certifies preservation of counterfactual candidate ordering and the selected action.

X-Cache gates cross-chunk block residual reuse with structure- and action-aware fingerprints and protects persistent KV updates, whereas RankSafe's reusable object is the exact shared prefix within one CEM candidate set and its acceptance condition is equality of planner-relevant computation, not a similarity threshold.

WorldCache adapts token skipping from curvature and drift to maintain rollout fidelity, whereas RankSafe leaves all action-conditioned suffix rollout computation intact and targets the distinct downstream quantity of CEM cost ordering and closed-loop first-action selection.

EfficientVLA combines layer pruning, visual-token selection, and temporal action-head feature caching in CogACT, whereas RankSafe changes no DINO-WM parameters or visual tokens and reuses only the exact observation/history prefix shared by counterfactual Wall-planning candidates.

DINO-WM supplies the latent visual dynamics and test-time action-sequence optimization but does not define a reusable prefix object or a planner-level cache-validity condition, which RankSafe makes explicit and tests with native latency and closed-loop action agreement.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: openalex:W7172558534 (collision_hits). The Gate, Not the Cache reports that at skip ratio 0.9 on LIBERO-Object, reuse and deletion fall to 0.68 and 0.31 respectively versus dense 1.00 when the next gate is harvested from the model's own accelerated forward; the collapse is invisible to the evaluated action-level detectors. This threatens any cache whose validity signal is self-contaminated across control steps. RankSafe instead computes a full candidate canary under the deterministic contract, falls back on mismatch, and directly measures first-action agreement and closed-loop success, so the hit is a provenance threat already covered by the candidate's guard rather than exact-mechanism overlap.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The provenance concern is addressed in `method_flow.steps` S3: the valid cache path uses a deterministic canary and falls back on mismatch, while the randomized-mask control disables fallback so gate contamination cannot be hidden. The `falsification_prediction` and `sub_claims.c3` fields make the required evidence downstream—rank inversions, first-action agreement, and closed-loop success—not merely a change in the gate itself, matching the Phase 3.2 verdict_rationale.
